column1: # The constitution already says editing engine/harness/lib or a hook is
# adversarial: those run in every session of every governed project, and a
# mistake there is silent. This is that sentence made mechanical, so felix
# classify and felix scope work on Felix the way they work on everything else.
# tier is advice: it says how carefully to look. `channel` is the stop, and it
# names what merging writes outside this tree that a revert cannot reach. A row
# with no channel classifies and stops nothing, which is what most of these are
# now: routine engine work on Felix was decided 2026-08-11 to need no approval,
# and until this column existed the table said the opposite of the doctrine and
# `confine` says what must stay true for a row NOT to fire. Bare means every
# changed line matches it. `count:` means at least as many matching lines as
# before — the right test for a verifier, which is judged by how much it checks
# and not by which lines it is written on.
# .github/workflows carries no row on purpose. It is an unconditional engine
# channel that no project can demote, because merging one runs the job holding
